statuses.title: Calibrated DP-FTRL resume silently changes sigma mid-horizon; drift guard disabled for calibrated runs
statuses.note: Fixed by pinning, not by recalibrating. _setup_training now passes resume_runtime.noise_multiplier into _calibrate_noise whenever the saved payload is a horizon process (_dp_trainer.py:1623-1635), and _calibrate_noise returns it verbatim before any calibration runs (:4566-4583, 'Restoring whole-horizon noise multiplier'). A new pre-setup guard _validate_horizon_resume_calibration (:5647-5678, called at :1180 before _setup_training) rejects calibration-mode drift AND privacy_target_epsilon drift on horizon resumes -- the gap OPQ-319 called out explicitly ('privacy_target_epsilon is absent from _current_values_for_drift entirely'). _current_values_for_drift still returns None for noise_multiplier under calibration (:5796-5807), but that is now harmless because the multiplier can no longer change. Reproduced end to end (mf_band bands=4, cyclic_poisson, target eps=3.0, 16 steps, checkpoints at 4/8/12): phase-1 nm=1.760345458984375; resume at every checkpoint returns ratio exactly 1.000000 and eps 2.998220940430295 unchanged (the original report measured ratios 1.0248-1.0909 here). Resuming with privacy_target_epsilon 3.0 -> 2.8 now raises CheckpointError at all three checkpoints. Verified that every reachable MF pairing (mf_identity/poisson, mf_identity/balls_in_bins, mf_band/cyclic_poisson, mf_band/b_min_sep, mf_blt/balls_in_bins) and gaussian/k_out_of_t all produce DpHorizonProcess, so no DP-FTRL configuration escapes the pin. The sigma-mixed MF noise buffer is therefore unreachable by construction.

statuses.title: Stop-at-epsilon not enforced per step for Monte-Carlo samplers (auto default for 5 of 6 MF mechanisms)
statuses.note: Fixed by refusing the configuration rather than by per-step evaluation -- the 'at minimum, refuse the configuration' branch of the fix sketch. _training_arguments.py:1241-1257 now raises ConfigurationError whenever privacy_noise_multiplier and privacy_target_epsilon are both set and (privacy_noise_mechanism != 'gaussian' or sampling_mode == 'k_out_of_t'). Verified by construction: mf_band/auto, mf_band/b_min_sep, mf_blt, mf_bisr, mf_bsr, mf_lambda_cgd, mf_identity/auto, mf_identity/balls_in_bins and gaussian/k_out_of_t are all REJECTED; only gaussian/poisson is ACCEPTED. Since _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS (:206-218) confines b_min_sep and balls_in_bins to MF mechanisms, the original failure config (mf_band + b_min_sep + nm=1.0 + target 0.5, which ran all 16 steps to eps 3.4072 against a 0.5 cap) can no longer be constructed. The residual MC carve-out at _dp_trainer.py:1248-1252 ('a.sampling_mode not in ("b_min_sep", "balls_in_bins")') and the log-boundary fallback at :4216-4225 are now dead code for those modes, and the in-loop stop at :2024 is a per-step integer comparison for the one surviving config. Whole-suite run (949 passed) confirms nothing depended on the old acceptance.

statuses.title: DataLoader prefetch advances the allocation cursor past global_step, misaligning accountant and sampler on resume
statuses.note: Fixed on both the save and the restore side. _TrainingContext gained sampler_step_offset (:255-258), snapshotted once in _inner_training_loop after get_train_dataloader() but before iter() so prefetch cannot pollute it (:1880-1886); _save_dp_runtime clamps the checkpointed cursor to min(sampler.consumed, global_step - sampler_step_offset) (:5284-5293); and _train_once additionally normalises legacy snapshots whose consumed exceeds global_step, with a warning (:1275-1292). Confirmed every reachable sampler serialises its cursor under the key 'consumed' (dpsgd _poisson.py:221, _k_out_of_t.py:183; dpftrl _b_min_sep.py:221, _balls_in_bins.py:223, _poisson.py:261, _sequential.py:138), so the `"consumed" in sampler_state` guard covers all of them rather than only the k-out-of-t path. A single sampler instance spans all epochs (one iter() for the whole run, :1879-1888), so the offset stays valid; _reset_state_for_batch_size_retry clears _ctx and _train_dataloader (:1364-1372) so an auto_find_microbatch_size retry cannot carry a stale cursor into a negative offset. Ran the full TestDPTrainerCheckpointing class (34 passed), including the three new regression tests that assert live_consumed_at_save[0] > 2 under num_workers=2/prefetch_factor=2 and payload.sampler_state['consumed'] == global_step, plus the ignore_data_skip rebase chain.

statuses.title: num_bins drift on resume resolved in favour of the sampler snapshot while the accountant uses the new value
statuses.note: The defect is gone structurally and is now also fail-closed. fc44ec8d replaced RandomAllocationSampler with KOutOfTSampler, whose amplification parameters are k/t/allocation rather than num_bins; both the runtime sampler (_dpftrl.py:308-330) and the accountant (_dp_trainer.py:4494-4525, dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t(k=sk['k'], t=n_steps, allocation=...)) read them from the same sampling_kwargs and total_steps, so the snapshot-vs-args split that OPQ-322 exploited no longer exists. e8f87cd1 then added the fail-closed restore guard the fix sketch asked for: _k_out_of_t.py:193-203 raises ConfigurationError when snapshot k, t or allocation differs from the template, mirroring the pre-existing num_samples guard. Verified live on a gaussian/k_out_of_t run (k=2, t=16, checkpoint at 8): resuming unchanged reproduces eps=3.1277903434589454, while per_device_train_batch_size 8->4 raises on 'sample_rate', k 2->4 and allocation block->total raise on 'horizon_process_state', and max_steps 16->24 raises on 'total_steps' -- all CheckpointError, none a warning. k_out_of_t is a DpHorizonProcess (confirmed at runtime), so _warn_on_arg_drift takes the horizon_resume branch (:5725-5735) and every dp_relevant field raises instead of logging the old 'heterogeneous RDP composition still yields a correct eps' claim, which no longer appears anywhere in the package or docs.

statuses.title: Four privacy-relevant kwargs dicts accept arbitrary keys silently; read keys are renames of the public parameters
statuses.note: Both halves fixed. b9b0a23e added per-dict allow-lists (_training_arguments.py:212-240) and a _validate_privacy_kwargs helper (:273-289) applied to clipping_kwargs, sampling_kwargs, privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs and noise_calibration_kwargs at :1339-1371, keyed by clipping_mode / sampling_mode / privacy_noise_mechanism as the fix sketch specified; and the trainer's read site was renamed to the underlying public factory names (_dp_trainer.py:4394-4396 now reads target_quantile / clipping_norm_max / gamma, not target_clipping_rate / norm_max). Verified by construction: the exact OPQ-324 payloads now raise -- clipping_kwargs={'target_clipping_rate':..,'norm_max':..} and {'learning_rate':0.2}, privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={'bounds':(-1,1)}, noise_calibration_kwargs={'minimum':0.5}, sampling_kwargs={'max_batchsize':8} -- while {'target_quantile':0.9,'clipping_norm_max':50.0} is accepted and reaches the factory. Cross-checked every _MECHANISM_KWARGS entry against inspect.signature of its strategy factory: all six match exactly with no extra and no missing keys, and default construction of all seven mechanisms still passes validation after _MECH_DEFAULTS merge. Residual cosmetic only: _MECHANISM_KWARGS['gaussian'] still lists 'bound', which is unconditionally rejected earlier at :1222-1228, so that entry is dead.

statuses.title: compute_loss_func and label_smoothing_factor silently ignored on the default eval path
statuses.note: The reported symptom is fixed: prediction_step's batched branch now routes through the custom loss (_dp_trainer.py:2719-2726) and rebuilds label-smoothed cross-entropy with a causal-LM-aware shift when no custom loss is set (:2728-2758, gated on the new self._is_causal_lm at :153-161). 19 new/existing contract tests pass. BUT the fix calls a callable whose documented contract is per-example-under-vmap (compute_per_example_loss docstring :2392-2395; docs/alignment/trainers.md:114 still says 'it runs inside vmap, so it must be a pure per-example op') with BATCH-ranked tensors, and validates nothing. For a rank-sensitive loss this silently produces a different eval objective than training -- the exact OPQ-325 failure scenario with a new cause. Reproduced: a per-example shifted causal-LM CE gives train objective 1.47203; default eval reports eval_loss 1.51315, while the same trainer with include_for_metrics=['loss'] reports 1.47203. Filed as finding 'compute_loss_func is invoked at two different tensor ranks'.

statuses.title: DPTrainer never consults ScheduleFreeState.x: schedule-free eval, checkpoints and saves use the wrong weight sequence
statuses.note: ebb2e2c3 added _published_params (:4670-4675), _use_published_functional_params (:4677-4689) and _use_published_model_params (:4691-4705) and wired every publication boundary: evaluate() (:3184), predict() (:3201), save_model() (:5031), checkpoint model artifacts (:5156), end-of-train restore (:1302), and _load_best_model re-seeds opt_state.x from the loaded best weights (:4920-4927). Resume reconstructs the training iterate y = (1-beta)*z + beta*x from the restored optimizer state (:5569-5573); beta round-trips through the serializer (verified: state_dict keys include 'beta', 'x.w', 'z.w'). Verified end to end with optim='schedule_free', base=adamw, beta=0.9, 8 steps: ||saved_checkpoint - x|| = 0.000e+00, ||saved_checkpoint - y|| = 1.017e-02, ||x - y|| = 1.017e-02, the post-train in-memory model equals x, and a resume reconstructs y to 0.000e+00. The trl SFT/DPO prediction_step overrides read ctx.trainable_params (_sft_trainer.py:672, _dpo_trainer.py:1317) and are reached only from evaluate()/predict(), i.e. inside the swap, so the stack-specific eval paths publish x too. Residual (not filed, low): a resumed run silently keeps the checkpoint's beta because ScheduleFreeState.update reads state.beta, so changing optim_args beta across a resume is ignored without warning.

statuses.title: _compile_with_fullgraph_fallback catches every Exception on the first call, masking non-compile failures
statuses.note: Two-step. f55c2a89 first narrowed the handler to torch._dynamo.exc.TorchDynamoException exactly as the fix sketch asked, so torch.OutOfMemoryError propagated to the trainer's OOM path. fae93a55 then deleted _compile_with_fullgraph_fallback outright and replaced it with _compile_strict_chunk (:209-219), which compiles only the tensor-only chunk kernel with fullgraph=True, dynamic=True and NO fallback and NO exception handling, so the reported double-execution and the misleading warning are both structurally unreachable. The removal is internally coherent: no dangling references (grep for _compile_with_fullgraph_fallback returns nothing), the docs were updated to drop the 'falls back with a warning' language (docs/reference/transformers.md:218, docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:216), and training_step's failure path was rebuilt around _synchronize_grad_failure (:1322-1348) which re-raises the original exception on a single process and MAX-all-reduces OOM vs non-OOM flags under DDP. The removal is NOT behaviourally free, however: what used to degrade to fullgraph=False now aborts the run, and I reproduced that torch_compile=True is unusable with Hugging Face models as a result. Filed as a separate finding.

findings.title: torch_compile=True aborts on the first training step for every Hugging Face model: the fullgraph fallback was deleted, not narrowed
findings.claim: fae93a55 (#979) replaced _compile_with_fullgraph_fallback with `_compile_strict_chunk`, which is a bare `torch.compile(fn, backend=backend, mode=mode, fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` with no exception handling. The compiled chunk kernel wraps `vmap(grad_and_value(per_example_loss))`, i.e. the whole model forward, and Hugging Face Transformers 5.15.1 calls `logger.warning_once` inside that forward (`use_return_dict` deprecation in configuration_utils, `loss_type=None` in modeling_utils). Dynamo rejects logging.Logger methods under fullgraph=True, so the first training step raises `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported` and the run dies. Before fae93a55 the same exception was caught (`except torch._dynamo.exc.TorchDynamoException` after f55c2a89 #891, `except Exception` at 4b13d82) and the step was retried under fullgraph=False, so the run completed.
findings.failure_scenario: `DPTrainer(model=LlamaForCausalLM(...), args=TrainingArguments(..., torch_compile=True))`; `trainer.train()` raises on step 1 with `Unsupported: logging.Logger method not supported for non-export cases ... Developer debug context: <Logger transformers.configuration_utils>.warning_once('`use_return_dict` is deprecated!...')`. Reproduced on a 2-layer LlamaForCausalLM and on the repo's own tiny GPT-2 + LoRA fixture, with clipping_mode fixed, adaptive and auto, on backends aot_eager and inductor -- 8/8 configurations fail. Monkeypatching `_compile_strict_chunk` back to fullgraph=False makes the identical run succeed (train_loss=3.64476 for all three clipping modes), proving the deleted fallback is the only thing that was making the feature work on HF models.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:209-219 — `def _compile_strict_chunk(fn, *, backend, mode): return torch.compile(fn, backend=backend, mode=mode, fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` (no try/except, no fallback)

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:4344-4368 — `_grad_compiler` returns `lambda fn: _compile_strict_chunk(fn, backend=backend, mode=mode)`; it is threaded into every clipping factory as `_chunk_compiler` (:4400, :4412, :4424)

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:588-601 — the compiled `_chunk_kernel` body is `vmapped = _vmap(_per_example_fn, ...); outputs = vmapped(kernel_clipping_norm, *chunk_args)`, i.e. the user's full model forward is inside the fullgraph region
git show fae93a55 — removes `_compile_with_fullgraph_fallback` (the `except torch._dynamo.exc.TorchDynamoException` handler that #891 had just corrected for OPQ-327) and adds `_compile_strict_chunk`

Reproduced: LlamaForCausalLM(2 layers, hidden 32) + apply_model_patches + torch_compile=True -> FAIL Unsupported for clipping_mode in {fixed, auto, adaptive}; same model with `_compile_strict_chunk` monkeypatched to fullgraph=False -> OK, train_loss=3.64476 in all three

packages/opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/test_compile_and_kernel_args.py:112-140 — `test_torch_compile_runs_poisson_training_strictly` is the only end-to-end compile test and it uses the synthetic `_TinyLM`, which emits no warning_once; the full transformers suite (949 passed, 16 skipped) is green with the feature broken
docs/reference/transformers.md:218 — `| torch_compile | bool | False | Compile each tensor-only microbatch gradient/clipping kernel with fullgraph=True. |` (no mention that HF models will abort)
findings.fix_sketch: Either restore a narrow fallback (catch torch._dynamo.exc.TorchDynamoException on the first call, log, and recompile the same chunk with fullgraph=False, while explicitly re-raising torch.OutOfMemoryError so _synchronize_grad_failure still sees it first-hand -- exactly the f55c2a89 shape), or keep fullgraph=True and add the HF logging functions to `torch._dynamo.config.ignore_logging_functions` inside `_grad_compiler` before compiling. Either way add an end-to-end regression test that runs DPTrainer(torch_compile=True) against a real transformers causal-LM (a 2-layer LlamaForCausalLM is enough) rather than a synthetic nn.Module, since that is the gap that let this ship.

findings.title: dynamic=True from the Poisson graph-reuse change makes clipping_mode="auto" + torch_compile crash even with no graph break
findings.claim: afa0247f (#989) added `dynamic=True` to `_compile_strict_chunk` to reuse one compiled graph across realized Poisson batch shapes. On the trainer's stack (torch.func.functional_call plus the opaque-patches `_reparametrize_module` recompute patch) that flag makes Dynamo's speculation log diverge for the AUTO-S clipping path specifically: `clipping_mode="auto"` + `torch_compile=True` aborts with `torch._dynamo.exc.SpeculationLogDivergence`, while `fixed` and `adaptive` compile and run on the identical model. The trigger is the flag, not the mode: with `dynamic` left unset (PyTorch's automatic dynamic shapes, the pre-#989 behaviour) or with `dynamic=False`, AUTO-S compiles and produces bit-identical results to eager.
findings.failure_scenario: A model with no graph breaks (so finding #1 does not mask this): `TrainingArguments(clipping_mode="auto", clipping_kwargs={"gamma":0.01}, torch_compile=True)`. `trainer.train()` raises `SpeculationLogDivergence: SpeculationLog diverged at index 626 ... Expected: opaque/api/patches/torch/checkpoint/reparametrize_recompute.py:37 (STORE_ATTR)`. Reproduced in a fresh process at per_device_train_batch_size in {2,6} with and without an explicit microbatch_size, on backends aot_eager and inductor -- 6/6 auto runs fail, 4/4 fixed and adaptive runs on the same model succeed. Variant sweep on the same run: fullgraph=True+dynamic=True FAIL, fullgraph=False+dynamic=True FAIL, fullgraph=True+dynamic=False OK (eps 2.866847, loss 0.881958), fullgraph=True+dynamic unset OK (identical numbers) -- so `dynamic=True` alone is the cause.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:209-219 — `torch.compile(fn, backend=backend, mode=mode, fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)`; `dynamic=True` was added by afa0247f
git show afa0247f — `perf(transformers): reuse compiled graphs across Poisson batch shapes (#989)`; the only source change is adding `dynamic=True`

Reproduced (fresh process each): clipping_mode=fixed compile=True OK eps=2.866847 loss=0.881958; clipping_mode=adaptive compile=True OK eps=11.811140 loss=0.881944; clipping_mode=auto compile=True FAILED SpeculationLogDivergence (same model, same seed, same data)

Traceback bottom frames: opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:601 vmapped(...) -> _clipped_grad.py:289 grad_and_value_fn -> opaque/api/patches/torch/checkpoint/saved_tensor_hooks_guard.py:45 -> _dp_trainer.py:2444 fmodel(params, **inputs) -> opaque/api/patches/torch/checkpoint/reparametrize_recompute.py:66 `_stack().append((module, params))`

Not reproducible at the engine level: `auto_clipped_grad(..., _chunk_compiler=torch.compile(..., fullgraph=True, dynamic=True))` over a plain tensor loss runs fine, so the divergence needs the trainer's functional_call + patch stack — which no test exercises (packages/opaque-engine/tests/clipping/test_compile_chunks.py and packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/clipping/test_compile.py both use pure tensor losses)

Counter-evidence that afa0247f is otherwise sound: with clipping_mode fixed/adaptive I verified compiled vs eager parameters agree to 0.000e+00 across batch shapes [1,3,1,2,1,3,3,4,5,1,4,2] and [3,0,0,2,1,1,0,1,2,1,2,1] (empty Poisson rounds included) and with microbatch remainders (bs=6/mbs=4), and empty batches never reach the compiled kernel because clipped_grad short-circuits first (_clipped_grad.py:322,337,348) and `_microbatch_accumulate_reduced`'s `range(0, 0, mb)` is empty — so the #808 empty-batch/step-shape concern is clean
findings.fix_sketch: Drop the explicit `dynamic=True` and let PyTorch's automatic dynamic shapes do the graph reuse (verified to keep AUTO-S working and to give identical numerics), or keep `dynamic=True` only when `clipping_mode != "auto"` until the AUTO-S `_scale_fn` path is made speculation-stable. Add an end-to-end parametrised test over clipping_mode in {fixed, adaptive, auto} that actually runs DPTrainer(torch_compile=True) — the current compile tests only build the args or use a pure-tensor loss.

findings.title: compute_loss_func is now invoked at two different tensor ranks; a per-example loss silently reports a different eval objective
findings.claim: The #819 fix makes the default (batched) eval path call `self._compute_loss_func(output, custom_labels)` on a batched ModelOutput, but training and the include_for_metrics=['loss'] eval path call the same callable under vmap with the leading batch dim stripped (`compute_per_example_loss`, :2452-2456, docstring at :2392-2395). Nothing validates the rank and nothing warns. A loss that indexes the leading axis -- the natural way to write a causal-LM objective under the documented per-example contract -- therefore computes a different quantity at eval than at training, and when sequence length equals vocab size it does so without raising. The token-weighted eval aggregation at :2946-2966 then multiplies that scalar by the batch's real-token count as if it were a per-token mean CE, compounding the error. docs/alignment/trainers.md:114 still states the SFT custom loss 'runs inside vmap, so it must be a pure per-example op', which is no longer true of the path SFTTrainer takes for loss_type='nll' (it delegates to `super().prediction_step` at _sft_trainer.py:647-650).
findings.failure_scenario: `compute_loss_func=lambda out, labels: F.cross_entropy(out['logits'][:-1], labels[1:])` (the documented per-example causal-LM shift) with eval_strategy='steps', metric_for_best_model='eval_loss', load_best_model_at_end=True. Reproduced on a causal-LM-shaped module with T=V=4: the training objective mean over the eval set is 1.47203; the default batched eval reports eval_loss=1.51315 (the function shifted along the BATCH axis and treated the sequence axis as the class axis, no exception); the same trainer with include_for_metrics=['loss'] reports 1.47203. Best-model selection, early stopping and every logged eval curve are driven by the 1.513 sequence. When T != V the same code path raises a shape error at eval instead, so a user who previously got a (wrong but harmless) built-in eval loss now gets a crash.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2719-2726 — `if self._compute_loss_func is not None: custom_labels = next((labels_kwargs[k] for k in label_keys if k in labels_kwargs), None); loss = self._compute_loss_func(output, custom_labels)` on the batched forward output

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2452-2456 — the training/per-example call: `labels = next((inputs[k] for k in self._label_names if k in inputs), None); loss = self._compute_loss_func(output, labels)` where `inputs` is 'One example's input dict (under vmap; the caller stripped the leading batch dim)' (:2409-2412)

Reproduced: train objective 1.4720335006713867; default eval_loss 1.5131527185440063; include_for_metrics=['loss'] eval_loss 1.472033441066742; direct batched call of the same fn 1.5981327295303345 with logits[:-1].shape=(3,4,4) and labels[1:].shape=(3,4)

docs/alignment/trainers.md:114 — 'A custom `compute_loss_func(outputs, labels) -> scalar` is honoured **only** on the `"nll"` path (it runs inside vmap, so it must be a pure per-example op — no `num_items_in_batch`)' — not updated by 25bb4ed7

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:647-650 — non-DFT loss types delegate to `super().prediction_step(...)`, so SFT nll + compute_loss_func lands on the batched call

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2946-2966 — the returned scalar is weighted by `int((labels[..., 1:] != _IGNORE_INDEX).sum())`, which only makes sense for a per-token-mean CE
The new tests added by 25bb4ed7 (test_trainer_contract.py) only use rank-agnostic losses (`F.cross_entropy(output['logits'], labels)` on 2-D logits), so the divergence is not covered
findings.fix_sketch: Make the contract single-ranked: on the batched branch, vmap the user callable over the batch (`torch.vmap`-free is fine -- a Python loop over the batch dim reusing one forward's outputs preserves the per-example contract and the existing token weighting), or, if the batched call is kept, validate it: assert the returned value is 0-dim and emit a one-shot RuntimeWarning naming the rank change the first time `_compute_loss_func` is called from `prediction_step`'s batched branch. Update docs/alignment/trainers.md:114 and the `compute_per_example_loss` docstring to state whichever convention wins, and add a regression test with a leading-axis-sensitive loss asserting that default eval and include_for_metrics=['loss'] agree.

delta_reviewed: Full delta for packages/opaque-transformers (41 commits, 4b13d82..12146ec4) plus the cross-package commits that land in its paths. Fix commits traced against the OPQ text, not the issue titles: 79acf31d/1794504b (OPQ-319), the _training_arguments rejection for OPQ-320, aabad3a0 (OPQ-321), e8f87cd1+fc44ec8d (OPQ-322), b9b0a23e+be7a1e39 (OPQ-324), 25bb4ed7 (OPQ-325), ebb2e2c3 (OPQ-326), f55c2a89+fae93a55 (OPQ-327). Non-fix delta reviewed in place: afa0247f (compiled-graph reuse across Poisson batch shapes -- audited hard against #808 empty-batch semantics: empty draws short-circuit in _clipped_grad before the compiled kernel and _microbatch_accumulate_reduced's loop range is empty, so no size-0 graph is ever traced; compiled vs eager parameters verified bit-identical across varying and empty batch shapes and microbatch remainders for fixed and adaptive clipping, but the flag broke AUTO-S -- filed); fae93a55 strict-chunk compilation and the new _synchronize_grad_failure DDP path (verified torch.OutOfMemoryError subclasses RuntimeError so the OOM classification still holds, and all ranks reach the same collectives); c0f95ced fused loss-only cross-entropy activation (reviewed the _fused_forward_uses_marker gating: it requires both a **kwargs-accepting top module and a submodule whose forward literally declares loss_only, so an unpatched custom model never receives the marker); 1633673e evaluation transfer overlap (read the new _CpuTransferPipeline: producer stream wait, record_stream on the source, event synchronize before the pinned->pageable copy, max_pending=2 -- correct by inspection but CUDA-only and unexercised here); c7bd1537/8a259dc8/587c1699/7edd41be/dcb202e5 eval memory and logits-free paths; fee28d2f checkpoint_barrier (confirmed all three stages are called symmetrically on every rank and that a stage failure aborts every rank rather than hanging); d8d43215 save_model barrier skip (confirmed _hub.push_to_hub returns early on non-zero ranks, so the skipped barrier is rank-symmetric); a624a34b DDP non-divisible population trim (now warned; sample-rate denominator and local_shard length both route through _effective_train_dataset_size); 029cc45f mf_band default sampler and the _cyclic_poisson_group_rate DDP conversion; 99f1874f tokenize_row staticmethod change (subclass overrides still bind correctly through `tokenize_fn = self.tokenize_row`);
